title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Assessment: Choose the Similarity Theorem
description: Show mastery by choosing the correct theorem from proportional side and included angle evidence.

questions.question: Triangles ABC and DEF have AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF. Which theorem proves the triangles are similar?
questions.explanation: All three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional, so the correct theorem is SSS Similarity.

questions.question: Two triangles have side pairs 9 and 12, 15 and 20, and the included angles between those sides are both 38 degrees. Which theorem proves similarity?
questions.explanation: The ratios 9/12 and 15/20 both simplify to 3/4, and the included angles are congruent. That is SAS Similarity.

questions.question: Which evidence is enough to prove triangle similarity by SSS?
options: Two pairs of sides are proportional and one angle is congruent.
Three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional.
Three pairs of sides are congruent.
questions.explanation: SSS Similarity needs three proportional corresponding side pairs.

questions.question: Which evidence is enough to prove triangle similarity by SAS?
options: Two proportional side pairs and the included angle congruent
Two proportional side pairs and any non-included angle congruent
Only one proportional side pair and one angle congruent
Three angle measures in one triangle
questions.explanation: SAS Similarity requires two proportional side pairs and the included angle between them.

questions.question: If two triangles have side ratios 4/6, 7/10, and 8/12, then SSS Similarity proves the triangles are similar.
questions.explanation: The ratios do not all match: 4/6 and 8/12 simplify to 2/3, but 7/10 is different.

questions.question: In SAS Similarity, the angle between the two proportional sides is called the ______ angle.
questions.explanation: The included angle is formed by the two sides being compared.

questions.question: Triangles PQR and XYZ have PQ/XY = 6/9 and PR/XZ = 10/15. Angle Q is congruent to angle Y, but angle Q is not between PQ and PR. Which conclusion is best?
options: Not enough evidence for SSS or SAS Similarity
questions.explanation: The given angle is not included between the two proportional side pairs, so SAS cannot be used. SSS cannot be used because the third side ratio is not given.

questions.question: Triangles have corresponding side lengths 7, 11, 13 and 21, 33, 39. What is the correct theorem choice?
options: Not enough evidence because no angles are given
Not similar because the triangles are different sizes
questions.explanation: The three ratios 7/21, 11/33, and 13/39 all equal 1/3. Three proportional side pairs prove SSS Similarity.

questions.question: If similar triangles have corresponding sides 8 and 20, then the ratio from the smaller triangle to the larger triangle is ______ in simplest form.
questions.explanation: The ratio from smaller to larger is 8/20, which simplifies to 2/5.

questions.question: A student chooses SAS Similarity because two side ratios match and one angle pair is congruent. What extra detail must the student verify?
questions.correctAnswer: The student must verify that the congruent angle is the included angle between the two proportional sides in both triangles.
questions.explanation: SAS Similarity only works when the congruent angle is between the two proportional sides.
